newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's complete landmine ban a world first.
newsitem.headline: Austria's complete landmine ban a world first.

text.p: Austria will become the first state to slap an unrestricted ban on anti-personnel landmines next year after a bill drafted by the Austrian Red Cross cleared the final parliamentary hurdle.
Austria's upper house the Bundesrat approved the ground-breaking law on Thursday night. It now requires President Thomas Klestil's signature before entering the statute book on January 1.
"Austria is the first country worldwide to declare a complete prohibition of these insidious weapons," Austrian Red Cross president Heinrich Treichl said.
"This is not only a moratorium or a limited restriction but means a total ban on anti-personnel landmines."

Austria's defence ministry welcomed the law, which prohibits the manufacture, use, possession and trade of both "dumb" and "smart" anti-personnel mines, detectable and fitted with a self-destruct mechanism.
"We are willing to support a worldwide ban on anti-personnel mines, especially given that over 80 percent of all victims are from the civilian population," a defence ministry spokesman said.
The Red Cross renewed its call for a global ban on the weapons, which have wreaked havoc in countries such as Angola and Cambodia where they were widely used by warring armies.
"We hope (Austria) will become an example for other governments to strengthen their struggle against the worldwide scourge of landmines," Treichl said.
